The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) in production environments presents a unique set of engineering challenges that differ significantly from traditional machine learning inference tasks. They generate text token-by-token, where each new token depends on the entire history of previously generated tokens. This sequential dependency creates a fundamental tension between latency (the time it takes to generate the first token and subsequent tokens) and throughput (the number of tokens or requests processed per second).

To resolve this tension, modern LLM inference servers have evolved a sophisticated stack of optimizations.
